_doc: Readable notes of the civic buildings of Pell's Crossing. Each advances its building's story and hints at the way through (items: items/civic.json note_<id>).

defs.title: St. Ansel's Daybook
defs.author: Rev. Joan Haskett
defs.body:
Day 6. Forty-one sleeping in the fellowship hall. Rosa has the pantry running like the Mile 9 at breakfast. I've chained the front doors - everyone comes and goes by the vestry now, round past the graves.
Day 8. A man off the roadblock crew sits in the back pew with his arm under his coat. He says it's a burn.
Day 9. The Okafors barricaded the pantry stair from below tonight and bolted the side door. They don't trust the people upstairs. I keep the pantry key myself: nobody goes hungry and nobody hoards.
Day 11. Vigil tonight. If anything happens I'll be up in the bell tower - the ladder's in the narthex. The bell carries all the way to the Tamsin road.

defs.title: Note on the Bell Frame
defs.author: J.H.
defs.body:
They are still singing downstairs. Or making the sound.
I rang until the rope parted, to draw them out of my church. Some went out through the vestry toward the bell. The rest are still sitting in the pews.
Rosa started coughing on Tuesday. She asked me to lock her in the pantry with the food so she couldn't hurt anyone, and I did. God forgive me. The key is on the nail.
The choir loft floor over the pantry stair has gone soft - you can drop through to the stair if you have to. The side door down there bolts from the inside.

defs.title: Pantry Sign-Out
defs.author: St. Ansel's Food Pantry
defs.body:
PANTRY SIGN-OUT - ONE BOX PER FAMILY PER DAY
Okafor x3 - 2 cans, rice
Lindqvist - 1 box
Brandt x2 - 4 cans
Merrow kids - milk powder (Rosa's own)
Tamsin crew x6 - 1 box (argued)

At the bottom, in red: ANYONE BITTEN REPORT TO REV. H - DO NOT HIDE IT
And in pencil, smaller: Rosa - 101.4 - moved into the pantry, her wish. Key with Rev. H.

defs.title: Northwoods Tab Book
defs.author: Marnie Lund
defs.body:
TABS CLOSED. EVERYTHING ON THE HOUSE TILL THE ROAD OPENS. - M.

Later, pressed hard:
BAR ROOM IS QUARANTINE. Front doors nailed from outside. Kitchen door locked. Do NOT open for anybody, not even if they say they're fine. Gus has the keys.
We come and go by the beer hatch on the north side. Keep it shut.

defs.title: Letter to Kari
defs.author: Marnie Lund
defs.body:
Kari,
The phones are dead so I'm writing it down. Your dad went down the beer hatch for water three nights ago and he came back up through the trapdoor behind the bar instead. I heard the cellar door. I locked the apartment and I haven't opened it since.
His keys are still on him. If anybody reads this: the safe's at the foot of our bed and the key is on Gus's ring. Take what you need. Then leave me be.
The back stairs door bolts from inside.
Love you. Mom

defs.title: Cordon Freight Manifest - Convoy 6
defs.author: Cordon Logistics
defs.body:
CORDON AUTHORITY - FREIGHT MANIFEST - CONVOY 6
Cordon Medical: fluconazole 150 mg x 40 cs / saline x 12 cs / body bags x 200
Destination: Waystation 9 / Harrow clinic
STATUS: HALTED AT MILE 9 ROADBLOCK. DRIVERS QUARTERED NORTHWOODS TAVERN.

Ballpoint along the margin: body bags. They brought BODY BAGS before they brought the medicine. - D.W.
And underneath: D. started shaking tonight. Marnie says the bar room is ours now.

defs.title: Postmaster's Daybook
defs.author: W. Benning, Postmaster
defs.body:
8/31 Cordon notice posted: no outgoing mail until further notice. People keep writing anyway. I keep sorting it.
9/03 Six registered cartons from Cordon Medical for Dr. Asante at the clinic. Locked them in the parcel cage. Asante never came to sign.
9/06 Dale and Lyle came back off Rural Route 2 after dark, both shaking. Put them in the dock with blankets and nailed the workroom door shut. The van is still at the bay.
9/07 Front doors locked. Box lobby left open for anybody waiting on a letter. The cage key hangs on the hook by my door. If the dock door is bolted, it's bolted from in here and I'm still in the building.
(pencil) Something got into the sorting room through the boxes. Don't go the lobby way. The only other way into the dock is the stair up from the carriers' room downstairs.

defs.title: Undeliverable Letter
defs.author: Annie Lindqvist
defs.body:
Dear Mom and Pop,
They say the mail is going out with the convoy so I'm writing even though the radio says the roads are shut. The larches turned early this year, gold all the way up the hollow. You'd have loved it.
There's a lot of people sick. Reverend Haskett has the church open and the Grange is taking families for the evacuation buses. We'll be on the first one. Don't worry about us.
Love, Annie

Stamped across it in purple: RETURN TO SENDER - CORDON HOLD.

defs.title: Grange Shelter Log
defs.author: Harold Sorensen, Grange Master
defs.body:
Evacuation assembly point per Cordon notice. 61 sheltered, beds for 64. Relief stock: 18 crates. Buses promised 0900.
Day 2. No buses. Cordon radio says tomorrow.
Day 3. Fever in four of them. Moved them upstairs into the old lodge room - SICK BAY. Piled the main stair hall full behind them so nobody wanders up or down that way. The nurses use the service stair from the kitchen.
Day 5. No buses. Locked the records room: the county lists, the last of the antifungals, the cash box. Key's on me, or on this desk if I'm upstairs.
Day 6. It isn't only upstairs. Cot 23.

defs.title: Sick Bay Chart
defs.author: Nurse E. Brandt
defs.body:
BED 1 - male, 40s - temp 103.2 - pale threads in both eyes.
BED 2 - Mrs. Nakamura - restrained per H.S. - stopped talking.
BED 4 - boy, 9 - asleep. Still himself.
The antifungals do nothing once it's in the eyes. Two boxes left in the records room - Harold keeps the key.
If they start humming together, get out by the fire door off the upper lobby. The balcony past it is rotten through - it's a drop to the porch, so mind it.

defs.title: Notice - Cordon Authority
defs.author: Cordon Authority
defs.body:
NOTICE
BY ORDER OF THE CORDON AUTHORITY
All residents of Pell's Crossing are to assemble at the GRANGE HALL for evacuation.
Bring one bag only. Pets will not be transported.
Persons who are sick, or who have been bitten, must report to the medical tent and will travel separately.
Do not approach anyone showing symptoms.

Scrawled across the bottom in marker: NO BUSES CAME.

defs.title: Lou's Radio Log
defs.author: Lou Petrakis
defs.body:
QSO LOG - 7.185 MHz
9/01 22:10 - Cordon traffic in the clear: 'containment units to Pell's Crossing, assembly at the Grange, transport for the uninfected only.'
9/02 06:45 - Waystation 9 net: 'no transport scheduled for Pell's Crossing.' So they lied to the Grange.
9/04 - Tried to raise the Grange on the CB. Nobody answers.
9/05 - Something walked on the roof all night. Front door's bolted, kitchen table's against the back one. Staying up with the rig.
9/06 - It's scratching at the far end of the trailer. The good stuff's in the gun cabinet; the key's taped to the rig.
